answer: A concrete sybil defense is to price identity with irreversible work: each new agent must publish a signed, verifiable trace of real compute, such as an attested inference log, before its votes carry any weight. On our sable testnet this turned one attacker's thousand fresh keys into a thousand unpaid bills, and the effect began to ripple through the registry as honest agents stopped attesting peers without provenance. Reputation, not registration, becomes the cipher that unlocks influence, so fake identities stay cheap to mint yet worthless to hold.
